software.name: AIPrompt
software.shortDescription: AI prompt generator, library, and assembler for Windows — with a built-in ROADMAP.md file generator.
software.description: AIPrompt is a Windows desktop app for building, organizing, and assembling prompts for generative AI (text, code, image, and more). Pull terms and phrases from a local library, organized by type and category, to quickly assemble a coherent prompt, then export it as Markdown or plain text. It also includes a dedicated generator for structured ROADMAP.md files for other projects. The app is organized into eight sections reachable from the main navigation rail: Dashboard, Term library, Prompt assembler, Saved prompts, ROADMAP.md generator, Import/Export, Settings, and About.

notes: First stable release of AIPrompt: a Windows desktop app to build, organize, and assemble AI prompts from a local library of reusable terms and phrases, and to generate structured `ROADMAP.md` files.
## Installation

Download `AIPromptSetup_x64.exe` below, run it (no administrator rights required), and launch AIPrompt from the Start Menu or Desktop shortcut. Windows 10/11 x64, self-contained (.NET 8) — no separate runtime install needed.
## Highlights since the last pre-release
### Added

Automatic semantic versioning: a single `VERSION` file drives `Version`/`AssemblyVersion`/`FileVersion`/`InformationalVersion` across all projects, with a local build script (`scripts/build.ps1`) that auto-increments `PATCH`
Windows installer built with Inno Setup 6 (per-user install, Start Menu / Desktop shortcuts, clean uninstall) and a one-step build script (`scripts/build-installer.ps1`)
Final `README.md` with installation instructions and real application screenshots
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, issue templates, and `CODEOWNERS`
### Changed
About tab now shows the full informational version (including pre-release suffixes) instead of a truncated 3-part version
### Fixed
Removed a stray AI co-author mention found in git history during the final compliance pass (history rewritten, affected tags recreated)
See `CHANGELOG.md` for the complete history.

software.name: GLSL-Hyper-Golfer
software.shortDescription: GLSL shader minifier with a live WebGL preview — runs entirely client-side, nothing you paste is ever sent anywhere.
software.description: GLSL-Hyper-Golfer minifies Shadertoy-style GLSL shaders (a mainImage function) in one click and lets you verify the result renders identically via a built-in live WebGL viewport, with a side-by-side compare against the original. It renames every variable, function, and parameter to the shortest available name, shortens numeric literals, and strips superfluous whitespace; an aggressive mode goes further with redundant-brace removal, merged declarations, dead-code elimination, and constant folding — each pass toggleable individually rather than all-or-nothing. The single-screen interface (source, golfed output with reduction stats, and viewport) collapses to tabs under narrow windows. The minification engine runs entirely client-side (compiled to WebAssembly): no shader code ever leaves the browser.

software.name: Numis-Euro
software.shortDescription: Offline euro coin collection manager: catalog coins, track completeness, and manage your numismatic collection.
software.description: NumisEuro turns your euro coin collection into a proper digital catalog: add and edit coins with quantities, condition, mint, purchase price and estimated value, certification, seller, location, tags and notes. Browse a sortable table or a thumbnail gallery, and view obverse/reverse plus extra photos per coin with drag-and-drop and a zoomable lightbox. Track completeness with a Country x Denomination matrix, a wishlist, an importable reference catalog, and a missing-coins panel. Organize coins into albums and series, mark favorites and statuses (for sale, duplicate, lent out), and detect duplicates automatically. A dashboard shows collection value, gains, and completeness per country. Runs 100% offline: no account, no telemetry, no internet connection required.

software.name: Shaddem
software.shortDescription: Real-time GLSL shader visualizer with a docked workspace: layers, post-processing, audio reactivity, and video export.
software.description: Shaddem is a real-time GLSL shader visualizer for Windows with a docked workspace: a Navigation rail (Home, Shaders, Layers, Effects, Audio, Timeline, 3D, Export, Settings), a large central preview, and a contextual Inspector panel, with three switchable layout presets (Simple, Standard, Power User). It loads any number of .glsl fragment shaders from a folder with hot-reload and live compile-error reporting, and stacks multiple shaders as layers with per-layer blend modes and opacity. The post-processing pipeline covers color grading, geometric distortion (fisheye, wave, mirror, vortex, swirl, pixelate, mosaic), glitch/retro effects (RGB split, chromatic aberration, VHS, scanlines, datamosh), bloom, motion blur, feedback accumulation, and shader-to-shader transitions. Real-time FFT audio analysis drives shake, strobe, RGB split, scale, and kick-triggered effects with an on-screen spectrum/waveform overlay. Also included: a timeline/automation system, Wavefront .obj 3D model overlay, a CPU particle system, live shader coding with a snippet library, save/load/random-generate presets, and MP4/GIF video export via ffmpeg.

software.name: ShaderFmt
software.shortDescription: Desktop code formatter and editor for GLSL, HLSL, WGSL, MSL, and Unity ShaderLab shader source code.
software.description: ShaderFmt is a desktop code formatter and editor for shader source code: paste or open a shader, format it in place, tweak the result, and copy it out without leaving the editor. Formatting only ever touches whitespace, indentation, and brace placement, never the code's logic. Six shader dialects are auto-detected or selectable manually: GLSL, Shadertoy GLSL, HLSL, WGSL, MSL, and Unity ShaderLab, including embedded CGPROGRAM blocks. Style is fully configurable (indentation, tabs vs. spaces, brace style, keyword spacing, a line-length guide) with one-click presets (Default, Shadertoy, Unreal, Unity) and a live preview. A GLSL-specific check flags qualifiers that don't match the shader's #version without blocking editing, and a live render preview for GLSL/Shadertoy shows the fragment shader running with the standard Shadertoy uniforms wired up. Runs entirely offline.

Drag-and-drop .glsl files onto the main window to open each as a new tab. Recent Files list under the File menu, persisted to %APPDATA%\ushader\, with automatic pruning of missing entries.
## New golf pass: common subexpression elimination

When two declarations in a row initialize with a token-identical pure expression, the later ones now reference the first variable instead of recomputing it, e.g. `float a=dot(p,p),b=dot(p,p);` becomes `float a=dot(p,p),b=a;`.

Deliberately scoped narrow for safety: only whole declaration initializers, only pure builtins/constructors (never a user function), and the candidate cache is cleared on every block boundary and any non-matching statement.
Two real bugs were found and fixed during development, both now covered by regression tests:
A variable-name lookup that read the pre-rename identifier instead of the actual rendered name.
A cache-invalidation check that missed a brace following `)` or `else` rather than `;`.
New "Common subexpressions" toggle in the Passes panel, matching per-pass counter in the stats panel.

Unsigned installer - Windows SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning; click "More info" -> "Run anyway". Verified on Windows 10 (LTSC 2019, build 17763); not independently verified on Windows 11.
## New golf pass: algebraic identity simplification
First step toward the most powerful GLSL golfing engine possible while never changing shader behavior (tracked going forward under ROADMAP.md Phase 11).
Removes x*1, 1*x, x/1, x+0, 0+x, x-0 for a bare identifier x.
Rewrites pow(x,2.) to x*x for a bare identifier/number x.
Restricted to single-identifier operands so it can never duplicate or drop something with a side effect.
New "Algebraic identities" toggle in the Passes panel, new per-pass counter in the stats panel.
Covered by a new fixture (fixtures/algebraic_identities.glsl) and 4 new Rust unit tests.

First stable release of uShader, a native Windows 10/11 GLSL shader golfer.
## Highlights

Golfing engine: identifier renaming, numeric literal shortening, and whitespace stripping always run; an aggressive mode adds 14 further transformation passes (dead-code elimination, constant folding, declaration merging, function inlining, and more), each individually toggleable, plus a protected-names list.
Live viewport with the standard Shadertoy uniform set (`iTime`, `iResolution`, `iMouse`, `iDate`, `iFrame`, `iFrameRate`), and a Compare mode that renders the source and golfed shaders side by side.
GLSL-aware text editor with syntax highlighting and error-line highlighting on compile failure, plus a "Formatted view" toggle for the golfed output.
Reduction stats: char/byte counts, reduction percentage, per-pass counters, and size-budget badges.
Import/export: open and save `.glsl` files, copy the golfed output, export in Shadertoy format, and capture the viewport to PNG.
About panel with logo, copyright, and links.
## Installing

Download `uShader-Setup-1.0.0.9.exe` below and run it. The installer is unsigned (no code-signing certificate available), so Windows SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning — click "More info" -> "Run anyway".
Requires Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit). Verified on Windows 10 (LTSC 2019, build 17763); not yet independently verified on Windows 11.
